tickets.title: Scope guard matches only intended paths
tickets.objective: scope_guard.sh admits paths it should deny and denies paths it should ignore; make its matching exact and give the hook its own tests.
acceptance: glob-to-regex match is anchored at BOTH ends; with scope portal/** the path backend/src/portal/routes.py is DENIED (regression test, this exact pair)
a path that does not resolve under CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR exits 0 (out-of-repo scratch is never the scope guard's business), compared after realpath so ../ traversal cannot escape scope
a missing or empty .claude/active-ticket fails CLOSED (deny) rather than open, with an explicit documented sentinel for deliberate unclaimed work
backend/tests/hooks/ drives the real hook with synthetic PreToolUse JSON over a table of (ticket, path, expect) pairs covering every ticket's scope in docs/tickets.json

each new hook test is written FIRST and demonstrated FAILING against current HEAD (the portal/** vs backend/src/portal/routes.py pair, the out-of-repo path, and the missing-claim case) before the hook is changed — this ticket authors its own gate, so a recorded red-then-green transition is what makes that gate meaningful
non_goals: No change to which paths any ticket's scope lists — this fixes the matcher, not the plan
No change to stop_guard/verify_gate session behaviour (T-13 owns that)

tickets.title: Session-scoped, append-only ticket claims
tickets.objective: Guards key off a single mutable untracked file with no notion of who claimed the ticket, so a second session in the same directory is told to finish or revert another session's work.
acceptance: a claim records ticket id + CLAUDE_SESSION_ID + UTC timestamp; stop_guard and verify_gate act ONLY on a claim owned by the current session
a second session in the same working directory is never blocked by another session's claim (fixture test asserting the observer case that fired on T-8, T-9 and T-11)
claim records are append-only and tracked in git, restoring the per-claim audit trail lost when .claude/active-ticket was untracked
guards refuse to honour a claim whose ticket already has a passing .claude/evidence/<id>.pass
worktree setup creates the checkout BEFORE the venv, and unlocks/prunes on exit; an unborn-HEAD worktree is treated as a setup failure to retry, not a reusable target
the cross-session test is demonstrated FAILING against current HEAD (a second session blocked by another session's claim) before the guards are changed, for the same reason as T-12
non_goals: No multi-agent scheduling or lock arbitration — this makes claims legible, it does not coordinate them

tickets.title: Verify commands cover their blast radius
tickets.objective: A ticket's verify runs only that ticket's own suite while its scope permits changes that break others; T-11's verify is additionally a script inside T-11's own scope.
acceptance: every ticket's verify runs its own suite plus every suite that imports from its scope paths (a reverse-dependency set), or the full suite where that is simpler
no ticket's verify command references a path inside that same ticket's scope — a gate is never authored by the work it gates
backend/tests/plan/ asserts both invariants above hold for EVERY ticket in docs/tickets.json, so a future ticket cannot reintroduce either
docs/tickets.json gains a status field the hooks maintain, so ticket progress is readable across sessions instead of inferred from evidence files
docs/TASKS.md re-synced to docs/tickets.json
the two plan invariants are demonstrated FAILING against current docs/tickets.json before any verify command is rewritten — including on this batch's own tickets, which must end compliant
non_goals: No widening or narrowing of any ticket's scope globs
No retroactive re-verification of already-closed tickets

tickets.title: Machine-enforce the human approval gate
tickets.objective: evals.report main() returns 0 unconditionally, so T-7's verify passes green with labels no human has approved; the project's one inviolable rule is its only unenforced one.
acceptance: python -m evals.report exits NON-ZERO while approval.status != APPROVED or approved_by/approved_date are empty
an explicit opt-in flag permits a draft run for development; T-7's verify command does not pass that flag
tests cover both directions: real unapproved fixture exits non-zero; a synthetic fully-approved fixture in tmp_path exits zero

the three existing not-yet-approved tripwire assertions are rewritten to assert the APPROVED invariants (report renders FINAL, metrics.approved is True, signoff fields non-empty) so a genuine human approval turns the suite green rather than red
docs/tickets.json T-7 verify updated to assert approval
non_goals: NEVER approves labels or fills signoff fields — that is the human step this ticket exists to protect
No threshold tuning and no change to the labeled set's contents

tickets.title: Test isolation and suite hygiene
tickets.objective: One shared database with per-test TRUNCATE means concurrent runs corrupt each other; the suite also rewrites a tracked file, and three conftest skip guards silently do nothing.
acceptance: each pytest process gets its own database or Postgres schema, derived from the xdist worker / worktree identity, so two concurrent full runs both pass (demonstrate by running two simultaneously)
no test writes into docs/ — the unapproved-report test reads committed artefacts read-only and generates into tmp_path; git status is clean after a full run, asserted by a test

the pytestmark skip guards in the graph, grounding and portal conftest.py files are moved somewhere they actually take effect (a pytest_collection_modifyitems hook, or per-module pytestmark) — pytest ignores conftest-level pytestmark for sibling test modules, so today they never fire
CI keeps its no-skip guard and gains a collected-count floor, so a suite that silently stops running is caught by number
non_goals: No new test cases for product behaviour — this is isolation and hygiene only
No weakening of any existing assertion to make a suite parallel-safe

tickets.title: Deploy verifier honours an exported DEPLOY_HOST
tickets.objective: verify_deploy.sh sources .env with set -a before reading DEPLOY_HOST, and .env defines it as an empty assignment, so an exported value is silently clobbered and the run falls to LOCAL mode while printing PASS.
acceptance: DEPLOY_HOST=<host> bash scripts/verify_deploy.sh takes the REMOTE branch; an exported value is never overwritten by sourcing .env (regression test with a fake env file reproducing the clobber)
local mode requires an explicit opt-in flag and can never be mistaken for droplet evidence; without it, an empty DEPLOY_HOST is a hard failure rather than a silent local PASS
T-11's acceptance criterion 1 can only be satisfied by a remote-mode run against a real droplet
docs/deploy.md and .env.example updated to match the corrected precedence
the clobber is reproduced FAILING against current HEAD (DEPLOY_HOST exported, run takes LOCAL and exits 0) before scripts/verify_deploy.sh is touched
non_goals: Does not create a droplet or perform a deploy — provisioning stays a human-authorised step
No change to the deploy stack itself (deploy/**)

tickets.title: Classifier errors stop masquerading as escalations
tickets.objective: run_classifier catches bare Exception and returns None, which is the pinned abstention condition and therefore a hard escalation trigger — so any bug in that path becomes a plausible-looking escalation, silently and unlogged.
acceptance: the except is narrowed to the API/timeout/parse/validation errors it actually intends to absorb; every swallow is logged with the exception type
a programming error raised inside the classifier path propagates instead of being converted to abstention (test asserts the exception escapes)
genuine abstention semantics are unchanged — a refusal or unparseable verdict still escalates, and every existing escalation test stays green
the three duplicated FakeLLMClient copies assert the classifier was consulted rather than only defaulting its response away, so an unanticipated call site is loud again
tickets.verify: uv run pytest backend/tests/escalation backend/tests/graph backend/tests/grounding -q
non_goals: No change to the hard-rule set, the combinator, or the confidence threshold
No change to which conditions escalate — only to which FAILURES are allowed to look like them

tickets.title: Bind the portal API contract
tickets.objective: portal/src/api.ts and backend/src/portal/schemas.py agree today purely by hand; nothing — no test, codegen step or CI job — fails if they drift, so a renamed field breaks only the live UI.
acceptance: the TypeScript request/response types are generated from the FastAPI OpenAPI schema, or a check asserts field-name, order and nullability parity between the two
regenerating against the current backend produces types byte-identical to what is committed
a deliberate backend field rename FAILS the check (demonstrate in the test, not by hand)
the check runs in CI on every push, not only when a human remembers
the parity check is demonstrated FAILING against a deliberately renamed backend field before being wired into CI
tickets.verify: uv run pytest backend/tests/portal -q && cd portal && npm run build && npm test
non_goals: No redesign of the API shape or the portal UI
No new endpoints

tickets.title: Versioned schema migrations
tickets.objective: A single ad-hoc _MIGRATIONS string now re-executes in full on every production container start, with no record of what has been applied; it survives only because its one statement happens to be idempotent.
acceptance: numbered migration files plus a schema_migrations ledger table recording what has been applied, so each migration runs exactly once
the existing runs.reasons column is expressed as the first migration; a database created before it still upgrades in place, and a fresh database ends in the identical schema (both proven by test)
container bootstrap applies only unapplied migrations rather than re-running the full list on every boot
a deliberately non-idempotent migration is applied exactly once across repeated init_schema calls (test)
a test proves a pre-existing database created WITHOUT runs.reasons is upgraded in place, run against a database built from the pre-T-8 schema
non_goals: No schema changes beyond formalising the existing runs.reasons migration
No ORM adoption — this is migration bookkeeping only

tickets.title: Escalation eval measures the real engine
tickets.objective: evals/report.py never imports EscalationEngine or run_classifier — it reimplements the precedence and fills the rest from three hand-authored replay tables, so its 1.0 scores grade a parallel implementation rather than the shipped engine.
acceptance: the report calls escalation.engine.EscalationEngine.evaluate directly; STUB_CLASSIFIER_VERDICTS, STUB_STRUCTURAL_REASON and STUB_ABSTENTION_IDS are deleted, not merely bypassed
the classifier half runs against a live LLMClient when OPENAI_API_KEY is present; without it the report FAILS rather than silently substituting fabricated verdicts
a test asserts the report and the engine cannot diverge — the report has no escalation decision logic of its own
the recommended threshold is swept over real classifier confidences, and the report states the sample size and date of the run that produced it
recall >= 0.95 on the hard-trigger subset is measured against the real engine, per T-7 acceptance 4
non_goals: Does not approve the labeled set — T-7's human gate still governs whether any number here is publishable
No relaxing of the >= 0.95 hard-trigger recall bar to make a real measurement pass
